(a 'queued' disposition here would mean the session was still busy)
ECHOED BACK       yes, after 4573ms
APPROVALS NEEDED  0 — the staging dir is OUTSIDE the repo, so reading the

WHY A NONCE       an agent can agree that it sees a file without reading one;
it cannot produce these bytes without having read them.

results.title: a pending interaction (permission / approval)

control.what: the turn producing durable transcript items at all (transcriptDelta on the same socket)
control.detail: 13 new transcript item(s) after the prompt; 19 delta frame(s) total

results.summary: no ask — this harness ran the tool without asking (permissive posture)
evidence: INTERACTIONS.LIST empty for this session after 21s
TOOL CALLS SEEN   bash, bash, bash, bash, bash, bash, bash, bash, bash, bash, bash
BLOCKED, NOT FAILED: the harness approved its own tool call, so the
product was never handed an ask to surface. That is a fact about this
rig's permission posture, not about the product's ask plane.

results.title: model / effort switch

results.summary: no product surface exists to switch model or effort mid-session
evidence: REQUESTED MODEL   (session default)
OBSERVED MODEL    (none — renders "requested, not yet observed")
OBSERVED EFFORT   (none)
DECLARATION       codex: configure unsupported ("model and effort are set at
thread start and per turn"); opencode: unsupported; terminal:
unsupported ("a TUI takes its model at launch"); grok: supported
for permissionMode ONLY, explicitly not model/effort.
PRODUCT SURFACE   no server or daemon code calls handle.configure(); sessions.sendText
carries no per-turn model or effort override either.
READING           the declaration and the behaviour agree, and the product does
not offer a switch it cannot honour. Nothing is broken and
nothing is proven — the cell is empty on BOTH arms, so this is
not a way in which headless is better or worse.

results.title: a provider error surfaced honestly
results.catalogRow: §6 provider overloaded / rate limit (pinned in the drivers; product surfacing is POD-2604)

control.what: this harness answering a normal question on this arm (probe 1)
control.detail: probe 1 PASSED, so a failure in this probe is attributable to the injected fault

results.summary: the bad model was ignored — the harness answered normally, so no error existed
evidence: INJECTED FAULT    model="podium-2777-no-such-model" on a opencode session
THE HARNESS       answered anyway: "Hello!"
PHASE / STATUS    phase=idle status=live
READING           the model string was not honoured as a fault, so the provider
never refused and there was no error to report. This probe
measured NOTHING about honest error surfacing, and says so
rather than scoring a FAIL for a fault that never fired.
A harder fault (revoked credential, unreachable base URL) is
what this cell needs, and it is not in this run.

results.title: interrupt a running turn
results.catalogRow: §1 interrupt a running turn (WIRED — declared capability, no conformance property)

control.what: the turn observed IN FLIGHT (phase=working, output growing) immediately before the interrupt
control.detail: phase=working, 26 preview frame(s), 0 chars on the transcript

evidence: WAS RUNNING       phase=working, 26 preview frame(s), 0 chars on the transcript
INTERRUPT SENT    {"ok":true}
SETTLED           NEVER — phase=working
TRANSCRIPT MARK   no item carries event:'interrupt'
TEXT AT INTERRUPT 0 chars → 0 chars at settle (durable transcript)
FRAMES AFTER      0 preview frame(s) arrived AFTER the interrupt was sent
PREVIEW CHARS     2105 at the interrupt → 2105 at settle
READING           generation STOPPED (no frame arrived after the call) but the
phase never left `working`. The turn is over and the product
still shows it running — a stuck state rather than an
unhonoured interrupt. Different defect, different owner.

results.title: resume after a kill
results.catalogRow: §4 resume() brings the CONVERSATION back, not just the ref (proven)

control.what: a conversation existing to restore — the pre-park turn answered with the secret
control.detail: the session repeated REMEMBER-BABU9L before it was parked

results.summary: resumed, but the conversation did not come back
evidence: SECRET            REMEMBER-BABU9L — spoken only in the pre-kill conversation
HIBERNATE         {"ok":true}; PARKED after 42ms (status=hibernated)
RESURRECT         {"ok":true}
→ back live?    NO — status=exited
RESUMEANDSEND     {"ok":true,"queued":true,"disposition":"queued"}
→ back live?    NO — status=exited
TWO VERBS         POD-2775 fixed resumeAndSend, not resurrect. A probe that drove
only resurrect would report that landed fix as broken.
RECALL            the secret never came back
SAME CONVERSATION YES — pointer conv_638af1d7-c1ed-4c30- unchanged across the park
ORIGINAL EXCHANGE present — the transcript still carries the prompt that planted the secret
WHY THREE CHECKS  a resume mutated to a STRANGER'S thread id passed 269 tests,
partly because the drive-level check was "both strings appear".
Containing the word is not being the conversation.
WHY THIS SHAPE    a healthy BLANK session carrying the old ref passes any
check that only asks whether resume returned ok.
NOT COVERED       recovery from an UNCLEAN death. sessions.kill REMOVES the row
(resurrect then answers 'unknown session'), so this drives the
hibernate/resurrect round trip a person actually performs.
